name: Lava Stone
physical: Crystal healers link it to a feeling of strength in the legs
Many people use it with oils for calm and comfort
summary: Lava Stone is porous volcanic rock used in crystal tradition for grounding, strength and steady courage, and popular in aromatherapy jewellery.
intro: Lava stone is solidified volcanic rock, usually basalt, that cooled from lava flows with gas bubbles trapped inside. The result is a dark, lightweight, pitted stone with a rough texture that feels like warm, crumbly charcoal. Black is the most common colour, but grey, brown and red-tinged pieces turn up, and beads are sometimes dyed bright colours. Because of its porous surface, lava stone soaks up liquids easily, which is why it is a favourite for diffuser bracelets and necklaces: a drop of essential oil lingers on the beads for days. It is inexpensive, hardy and easy to find, and it carries the raw fire of the volcano that made it.
history: Lava has been used as building and tool material since antiquity. Romans quarried volcanic rock near Vesuvius and Etna for paving stones, millstones and construction, and Hawaiian and Polynesian cultures shaped basalt into adzes and carvings. In Hawaii, lava is sacred to Pele, goddess of volcanoes, and there is a well-known belief that removing lava rocks from the islands brings misfortune. Millstones carved from vesicular lava were exported across Europe from the Eifel region. Modern lava stone jewellery gained popularity in the 2000s with the rise of aromatherapy beads. In the crystal world, lava stone is cherished for its physical link to the earth's molten core.
meaning: Lava stone is the earthy fire stone: grounded yet powerful. Practitioners associate it with the Root, Sacral and Earth Star, saying it connects you to the earth's deep energy and encourages courage, stamina and emotional steadiness. It is often recommended for people who feel anxious, scattered or easily thrown off balance, because its weight and roughness bring attention back to the body. The volcano origin gives it associations with transformation and the power of creation from destruction. Many use it for working through anger constructively, finding strength without explosion. It is also valued for its porous texture, which makes it perfect to pair with essential oils for a sensory grounding ritual. These associations are traditional, not medical claims.
howToUse: Wear a lava bead bracelet with a drop of lavender or cedarwood oil for scent-based calm, and refresh the oil every few days. Hold a piece during meditation, focusing on its rough surface and weight. Keep a larger chunk near your door or in a plant pot for grounding. In the bedroom, place a small stone with a drop of oil by the bed. Include lava stone in a grid for stability and fiery motivation. Always check oils are skin-safe if you wear the beads against skin.
care: Lava stone is sturdy but porous. Avoid soaking it for long, as it will absorb water and take time to dry, and avoid cleaning with oils you do not want to linger. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or a rest on selenite. Sunlight is safe. If used with essential oils, wipe the surface with a dry cloth before switching scents, or use separate beads for different oils. Store in a pouch, as rough surfaces can scratch softer stones. Dry thoroughly before storing.
identify: Genuine lava stone is lightweight with visible bubble holes, a matte rough surface and a dark grey to black colour. It should look and feel like a pitted volcanic rock. Dyed beads are common, so rubbing with a damp white cloth may show colour transfer. Imitations include moulded cement, resin or pumice painted black, which feel heavier or too uniform. Real lava stone often has uneven shapes, tiny crystals of olivine or feldspar and variable pore sizes.

faq.q: What is lava stone used for?
faq.a: In crystal tradition it is used for grounding, strength and steady courage. It is also very popular for aromatherapy jewellery because its porous surface holds essential oils.
Yes, it will not dissolve, but it is porous and absorbs water, so it takes time to dry. A quick rinse is fine; avoid long soaks and dry thoroughly to prevent trapped moisture.

faq.q: Is lava stone really from a volcano?
faq.a: Yes. It is solidified lava, normally basalt, with gas bubbles locked inside as it cooled. Some beads are dyed or reconstituted, so check for colour transfer if you want an untreated piece.
